Inwards
IN-werdz
noun
From Old English inneweard, that which is within, rendering the Hebrew qereb, the inner part or midst. It names the entrails and inner organs of the sacrificial beast, which were washed with water and offered with the fat upon the altar.

Biblical Definition

The inwards were the inner parts — the entrails and viscera — of the beast brought to the altar, dealt with according to a careful rule in the law of the offerings. The fat that covered them was burnt to the LORD (Exo 29:13; Lev 3:3), and the inwards themselves, together with the legs, were washed with water before the whole was consumed: “But his inwards and his legs shall he wash in water: and the priest shall burn all on the altar” (Lev 1:9). In the sin offering the bullock’s skin, flesh, head, legs, and inwards and dung were carried forth without the camp (Lev 4:11). Two things the inwards teach. First, that God lays open the inner man: the offering was not accepted with its inwards hidden and unwashed, but everything within was exposed, cleansed, and given up. Nothing secret was withheld from His eye. Second, that the whole man, and not the outward parts alone, must be sanctified; the inwards washed with water figure the cleansing of the conscience and the hidden thoughts. The LORD looketh not on the outward appearance but on the heart, and He will have the inner man laid bare before Him and purged. What water did to the inwards of the beast, the blood of Christ and the washing of the word do to the inward parts of His people, that they may be an offering of a sweet savour unto God.

Webster 1828 Definition

The inner parts or entrails of a sacrificial beast, washed with water and offered upon the altar.

expand to see more

INWARDS, the inner parts, entrails, or viscera of a beast offered in sacrifice.

The fat covering the inwards was burnt upon the altar as the LORD’s portion.

The inwards themselves, with the legs, were washed with water before being consumed.

In the sin offering the inwards were carried forth without the camp with the rest of the beast.

The word is from Old English inneweard, that which is within.

Key Scripture

Exo 29:13 — "And thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inwards, and the caul that is above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and burn them upon the altar."

Lev 1:9 — "But his inwards and his legs shall he wash in water: and the priest shall burn all on the altar, to be a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD."

Lev 3:3 — "And he shall offer of the sacrifice of the peace offering an offering made by fire unto the LORD; the fat that covereth the inwards, and all the fat that is upon the inwards,"

Lev 4:11 — "And the skin of the bullock, and all his flesh, with his head, and with his legs, and his inwards, and his dung,"

Modern Corruption

A part of the offering, not a contested doctrine; it recovers that God lays open and cleanses the whole inner man.

expand to see more

The inwards rebuke a religion content with an outward show while the hidden parts remain unwashed. The age is careful of appearances and careless of the heart; it polishes the outside of the cup and leaves the within full of uncleanness. But the law that washed the inwards of the offering testifies that God will not accept a sacrifice whose inner parts are hidden and defiled.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the whole inner man must be laid open and cleansed before God. The inwards were washed with water and given wholly to the altar; so the conscience and the hidden thoughts must be purged by the blood of Christ and the washing of the word, that the worshipper may be an offering of a sweet savour.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The inner parts of the offering, washed and consumed, figuring the whole inner man laid open and cleansed before God.

expand to see more

Inwards — the entrails and inner parts of the sacrificial beast (Exo 29:13).

The inwards, with the legs, were washed with water before burning (Lev 1:9).

The fat that covered the inwards was burnt as the LORD’s portion (Lev 3:3).

In the sin offering they were carried forth without the camp (Lev 4:11).

The word is Old English inneweard, that which is within.

Usage

"The inwards were washed with water; nothing hidden was offered unclean to God."

"The LORD looketh on the heart and will have the inner man laid open before Him."

"As water cleansed the inwards, so the blood of Christ purges the conscience within."
